title: What If It Rained for Two Million Years? Earth Did That

scenes.text: What if Earth had a two-million-year rainy season? It really did.
About 234 million years ago, four pulses of volcanic eruptions released huge amounts of carbon dioxide.
Temperatures rose, humidity jumped, and a mega monsoon climate set in across a mostly hot, dry world.
Rivers and lakes swelled. Some lakes grew deeper as their oxygen fell and animal life shrank.
Humidity-loving plants spread, and turtles, big amphibians and early dinosaurs thrived in the wetter lands.
The first dinosaurs were cat-sized then. They began a reign that lasted about 166 million years.
